title: The one who left in anger
word: The one who left in anger
hook: Yunus gives up on his people, walks off in anger, boards a crowded ship, and is thrown into the sea
carry: walking away is also a choice

segments.voice: Yesterday, Isa, the Messiah and healer, who did it all by Allah's leave. That was your line. Did something good come through you? Today, a new prophet and a very different mood. Day seventy-five.

Ten explanations. Patience, and more patience. Every approach tried, and still nobody listens. Then the keys come off the hook, and the door closes, not slammed, just closed hard. That's where this story starts. A prophet named Yunus has been calling his people to Allah, and they won't have it. And the Qur'an says, simply, he went off in anger. He heads for the sea and boards a ship. Anywhere but here. Then, out at sea, things go wrong.
screen: `THEY WON'T LISTEN.` → `HE WENT OFF IN ANGER.` → `HE BOARDS A SHIP.`

segments.voice: The Qur'an tells this story in pieces, in several surahs. In Surah Al-Anbiya it gives him a nickname, in Pickthall's words: “And (mention) Dhu'n-Nun, when he went off in anger.” Dhu n-Nun: the one of the fish. In Surah As-Saffat, the ship: “When he fled unto the laden ship.” Fled. The Arabic word used here is the one for a runaway slave leaving his master. That's how the text names what he did. Commentators explain that Yunus left his people before Allah had given him leave to go. His frustration was understandable. His leaving was still a choice. Then trouble at sea. The Qur'an doesn't describe it; commentators say the ship was in danger and someone had to go over the side. They cast lots, and the lot falls on Yunus. He's thrown into the sea, and a great fish swallows him. The Qur'an says he was blameworthy at that moment. It doesn't pretend otherwise. And yet Yunus is still a prophet, honored by name. The tenth surah is called Yunus. And the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari to have said that no one should say he is better than Yunus, son of Matta. The one who walked out is not written off. Another surah even tells the Prophet: be patient, and don't be like the companion of the fish. The lesson is gentle: Yunus is a warning and a beloved prophet at once. Jews and Christians know him too, as Jonah, from the Hebrew Bible. For now, leave him where the Qur'an leaves him today: in the dark, inside the fish.
screen: `DHU N-NUN: THE ONE OF THE FISH.` · `HE FLED UNTO THE LADEN SHIP.` · `THE LOTS FALL ON YUNUS.` · `NO ONE IS BETTER THAN YUNUS.` · then, large: `WALKING AWAY IS ALSO A CHOICE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: notice where you walked out angry. Settle, and breathe. Think of a place, a person, a job, a conversation, where you left in frustration. Maybe you were right to be frustrated. Don't argue that. Just notice the moment of leaving. What did it feel like in your body? What did you tell yourself as you went? Was it a choice, or did it feel like the only option? If you pray, you can ask Allah to show you what you couldn't see then. The bell holds the time.
The one who left in anger. Yunus, Dhu n-Nun, walks away from his people before he's told to, and ends up in the sea.
screen: `THE ONE WHO LEFT IN ANGER — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: walking away is also a choice. Today, if you feel the urge to walk out of something, stop for one breath and ask: am I choosing this, or just fleeing? Tomorrow, what Yunus says in the dark. Day seventy-five.

howItsDone: Muslims read the story of Yunus in Surahs Yunus, Al-Anbiya, As-Saffat and Al-Qalam, and honor him as a prophet whose story teaches patience with people and turning back to Allah.

myth: Yunus left his people before Allah gave him leave
commentators explain his leaving this way; the Qur'an says he went off in anger (21:87).
after the fish, the Qur'an stops calling Yunus a prophet
he remains an honored prophet, and a surah bears his name.
the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said no one should claim to be better than Yunus

fork.setup: Yunus has called his people again and again, and they won't listen. what does he do?
options: keep calling, and wait for Allah's word.
leave them, in anger, on the first ship out.
fork.reveal: he went off in anger (21:87) and fled unto the laden ship (37:140), and the Qur'an calls him blameworthy for it.

original.note: Arabic: the one of the fish, Yunus's name in 21:87.

trapdoor: what you thought: a man swallowed by a whale.
what it means: a prophet who gave up on his people and walked out before he was told to, and wasn't written off for it.
what a scholar hears: 37:140 uses abaqa, the word for a slave running from his master, for Yunus's flight; and still a hadith forbids anyone to say they are better than him.
